target: Sun's disjoint-coset conjecture (Internat. J. Math. 17 (2006) Conjecture 1.2) at k = 5 for EVERY group: if a_1G_1, ..., a_5G_5 are pairwise disjoint left cosets of subgroups of finite index in a group G, then gcd([G:G_i],[G:G_j]) >= 5 for some i < j; or an exact counterexample.

exact_statement.groups: arbitrary groups G (not only Z); subgroups G_i of finite index, possibly equal; cosets pairwise disjoint (not a cover)
exact_statement.sharpness: 5 cosets of one subgroup of index 5

primary.conjecture: Sun 2006 Conjecture 1.2 (arXiv math/0501451v4); Remark 1.5(a): open even for Z (later settled for Z up to k<=20 by O'Bryant)
primary.known_groups: k=2 and p-groups (Sun 2006); k=3,4 for all groups (Zhu, arXiv 0807.2207; reproved Margolis-Schnabel arXiv 1803.03569, Beitr. Algebra Geom. 60 (2019), incl. Props 4.2, 4.3, 4.5 and Theorem B for n<=4)

initial_representation: R1 (screen, unreviewed): k=5 for groups is equivalent to Core(5): no group has subgroups U_1..U_5 of indices 4r_1..4r_5 with r_i pairwise coprime and pairwise disjoint cosets; pairwise data alpha_ij in {1,2,3} with [G:U_i cap U_j] = 4 r_i r_j alpha_ij; published Margolis-Schnabel rules (Lemma 3.7, 3.10, Cor 3.9, 3.11, Props 4.2/4.3/4.5) plus candidate lemmas N1-N3; reduce to an exact finite list of alpha-labelled patterns (with the at-most-one special subgroups r even / 3|r) and attack survivors by written proofs.
first_obligation: Before any substantive work: re-run targeted arXiv/OpenAlex/DataCite searches for k=5 group claims (stop on a prior claim) and record them.
Read Margolis-Schnabel pp.8-10 (Props 4.2, 4.3, 4.5, Lemma 4.4 caveat alpha != 2, Cor 3.11 swap) and freeze R0-R3 with exact citations and written proofs in the lane README.
State every rule as a lemma with explicit hypotheses (published ones cited exactly; N1-N3 and any new lemma with full written proofs).

Enumerate alpha-labellings with special-subgroup choices up to relabelling in a tiny exact program (Python, deterministic, kilobyte outputs); output a certificate per pattern (which rule kills it) or the survivor list.
Attack survivors by written proofs; any counterexample candidate must be an explicit finite group with explicit cosets.
controls: The same rule engine reproduces Props 4.2, 4.3, 4.5 (k=4 statements).
Known realisable configurations survive every rule: Menon's A_5 (6,6,6,10,15) and C_2 x S_4 examples, all four-subgroup subconfigurations, k cosets of one subgroup.
Rules give cyclic groups all alpha = 1 and abelian groups alpha <= 2.
Mutating a label in a pattern certificate breaks it for the intended reason.
acceptance: GATE: a complete written proof of Core(5) (hence k=5 for all groups) covering every pattern, OR an exact counterexample verified by two independent exact checkers plus a parent recomputation; independent parent re-derivation of the reductions and of every rule used; hostile reviews from both CLI families (Codex gpt-6.1-sol and Claude claude-opus-5-5); post-result priority audit. A finite or partial reduction, a small-group search, or a permutation-group search is NOT the gate.
